nodes.title: Commuting block coordinates
nodes.statement: Choose occurrence labels for m. A degree −1 commuting map from the VN interval [t,u] to [s,v] exists with one free scalar precisely when s<t≤v+1≤u; otherwise that block is zero. Within an allowed block its scalar is constant wherever the target basis vector of degree a−1 exists. Consequently centralizer(standardPair m) is linearly equivalent to one independent complex coordinate for each allowed ordered occurrence pair. At degree a+1→a the coordinate occupies exactly the row of the target occurrence and column of the source occurrence.
hypotheses: Integer endpoints; finite multisets. For graded operator statements, finite dimensional complex spaces with finite support integer grading.
proofSteps: In interval bases extend matrix coefficients by zero outside both blocks. Commutativity equates the coefficient at degree a with that at degree a+1. The two boundary zero equations force the strict endpoint and overlap inequalities. Conversely a constant scalar on a permitted overlap satisfies all equations. Apply this independently to every ordered occurrence pair, including repeated intervals with different labels.

nodes.title: Polynomial Zariski topology
nodes.statement: On C^n use the topology generated by polynomial nonvanishing loci. On a finite dimensional vector space transport this topology through a complex basis; prove independence of the basis and compatibility with linear maps and subspaces. ZariskiOpenDense(P,U) means U is both open and dense in centralizer(P) for this topology, including the zero dimensional case.
hypotheses: Integer endpoints; finite multisets. For graded operator statements, finite dimensional complex spaces with finite support integer grading.
proofSteps: Invertible linear coordinate changes pull polynomials back to polynomials. A nonzero polynomial over the infinite field C has a nonzero evaluation, by induction on the number of variables. Products of finitely many nonzero polynomials remain nonzero, so nonempty principal opens meet. This proves irreducibility and finite intersection of dense opens. For a surjective linear map choose a section and a kernel complement: the preimage of a nonempty open dense set is open dense. Do not install the Euclidean topology for these predicates.

nodes.title: Generic commuting type
nodes.statement: For a finite graded pair P, maximize simultaneously the ranks of every graded path of the opposite commuting operator.
